## Defaults

<!-- Generated by lib/build-roles/src/cli.ts from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Fail a build only for a broken Law.** Fail builds only for a Law or mechanically provable correctness constraint; warn on Defaults, inform on Preferences, and keep Tooling rules easy to change. [`core/fail-a-build-only-for-a-broken-law.md`]
- **Fix the root cause, not the symptom.** Fix the boundary, model, config, or dependency direction causing the problem rather than adding a workaround shim. [`coding/fix-the-root-cause-not-the-symptom.md`]
- **Prove the invariant even when a library provides the capability.** Even when a library provides a capability, still prove the invariant, pick the right boundary, and account for the provider's failure model. [`coding/prove-the-invariant-even-when-a-library-provides-the-capability.md`]
- **Add a package only for commodity machinery.** Add a package for commodity machinery; write small, well-understood product logic yourself when a package's scope, cost, maintenance, or semantic mismatch outweighs the code it replaces. [`coding/add-a-package-only-for-commodity-machinery.md`]
- **Wrap a dependency only when the wrapper adds meaning.** Never wrap a library or generated client one-for-one (nor just because it is generated); add a wrapper only when it combines calls into one capability, adds non-trivial policy or orchestration, or translates an external model owned elsewhere, changing independently, or needing a test abstraction. [`coding/wrap-a-dependency-only-when-the-wrapper-adds-meaning.md`]
- **Add an abstraction only at a real boundary.** Add an interface, port, adapter, or indirection only at a real boundary: I/O, plausible variability (a second implementation), another owner, a runtime or cross-module boundary, or a test that needs it. [`coding/add-an-abstraction-only-at-a-real-boundary.md`]
- **Keep code local until it is shared.** Keep code beside its one consumer, and promote it only when it has more than one real consumer, stable enough ownership, and clearer value shared than duplicated. [`coding/keep-code-local-until-it-is-shared.md`]
- **Keep shared code with the feature that owns it.** Keep code used by multiple consumers inside its owning feature behind its public entry point (on the backend, its published contract); move to a shared folder only when no single feature owns it. [`coding/keep-shared-code-with-the-feature-that-owns-it.md`]
- **Register dependencies explicitly.** Register and wire every dependency by name in code a reader can open; do not use assembly scanning, reflection conventions, or provider discovery. [`coding/register-dependencies-explicitly.md`]
- **Import from the file that owns the code.** Import from the file that defines a thing; do not add barrel or re-export files, and delete the old file when code moves. [`coding/import-from-the-file-that-owns-the-code.md`]
- **Use plain data and pure functions by default.** Model data as plain types and change it with pure functions; put methods on an entity only where they protect its lifecycle invariants, and do not build inheritance-heavy models. [`coding/use-plain-data-and-pure-functions-by-default.md`]
- **Extract a helper only after the pattern repeats.** Leave similar lines duplicated until the pattern has shown itself; three similar lines beat a helper extracted the first time the shape appears. [`coding/extract-a-helper-only-after-the-pattern-repeats.md`]
- **Write code that reads top to bottom.** Write a procedure as statements in the order they run, so a reader understands each line without holding an abstraction in their head. [`coding/write-code-that-reads-top-to-bottom.md`]
- **Comment only to explain why.** Write a comment only to explain why: a constraint that is not obvious, a design decision, or a real trap; never to restate what the code says, and when in doubt leave it out. [`coding/comment-only-to-explain-why.md`]
- **Model the real type of every value.** Give every value its real type: never `any`, `object`, `object?`, or `dynamic`, and `unknown` only at a boundary until parsed. [`coding/model-the-real-type-of-every-value.md`]
- **Use a dictionary only for dynamic keys.** Use `Dictionary` or `Record<string, unknown>` only for data whose keys are not known at compile time; when the keys are known, use a record or a named type. [`coding/use-a-dictionary-only-for-dynamic-keys.md`]
- **Model each state explicitly in TypeScript.** Model each state a value can be in as its own case of a union, instead of optional fields read with `?.` and `??`. [`coding/model-each-state-explicitly-in-typescript.md`]
- **Declare TypeScript functions as const.** Declare a TypeScript function as a `const`. [`coding/declare-typescript-functions-as-const.md`]
- **Handle a new enum value in every consumer.** When you add an enum value, status, or type constant, find every consumer (switches, filter arrays, display logic, serialisation) and handle the new value in each, reading outside the diff. [`coding/handle-a-new-enum-value-in-every-consumer.md`]
- **Report data safety findings before style.** Review data safety and races first (a check before a write with no atomic condition in the write, find-or-create with no unique index), then style and consistency, and do not mix the two in the findings. [`coding/report-data-safety-findings-before-style.md`]
- **Fix mechanical findings without asking.** In a fix-enabled review, fix mechanical findings (dead code, stale comments, missing includes, unused variables) without asking, make design fixes settled by facts and rules regardless of size, and ask the user only what those cannot settle (e.g., removing user-facing features) in one batched question with recommendations. [`coding/fix-mechanical-findings-without-asking.md`]
- **Leave harmless redundancy out of review findings.** Do not report redundancy that helps a reader, a threshold value tuned empirically, or an assertion that could theoretically be tighter but already covers the behaviour. [`coding/leave-harmless-redundancy-out-of-review-findings.md`]
- **Enforce at the narrowest owner with enough information.** Put enforcement of an invariant in the narrowest owner that has all the information the invariant needs. [`invariants/enforce-at-the-narrowest-owner-with-enough-information.md`]
- **Add a type to enforce an invariant only when it earns its place.** Add a new type for an invariant only when it shrinks representable states, centralises a legal transition, or owns a real consistency boundary. [`invariants/add-a-type-to-enforce-an-invariant-only-when-it-earns-its-place.md`]
- **Rule out an invalid value with the smallest tool.** Rule out invalid values with the smallest tool that suffices: a precise static type or discriminated union, runtime schema validation at untrusted boundaries, and a parser or value object only when it prevents invalid construction or removes duplicated validation. [`invariants/rule-out-an-invalid-value-with-the-smallest-tool.md`]
- **Fix a shown race with the smallest mechanism.** For a demonstrated race, use the smallest mechanism that holds the invariant, in order: last-writer-wins (if harmless), DB constraint, single atomic conditional write (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` / `UPDATE ... WHERE ... RETURNING`), version/concurrency token, short transaction at appropriate isolation, row lock, and only last an established advisory/distributed lock library when no row, constraint, or atomic statement can represent the coordination. [`invariants/fix-a-shown-race-with-the-smallest-mechanism.md`]
- **Use an advisory lock only for a domain identity.** Use an advisory lock only when the thing locked is a real domain identity that no row, constraint, or atomic statement can represent; it is not the way to make an operation idempotent or to suppress duplicates. [`invariants/use-an-advisory-lock-only-for-a-domain-identity.md`]
- **Design every lock's scope, timeout, and loss handling.** For every lock, design its name, scope, timeout, cancellation, release, and what happens if the connection or handle is lost while work is still running. [`invariants/design-every-locks-scope-timeout-and-loss-handling.md`]
- **Define idempotency key meaning in the application.** Define an idempotency key's scope, fingerprint, replay policy, and expiry in the application, while the database or an established library reserves and arbitrates it; it is not duplicate-content detection. [`invariants/define-idempotency-key-meaning-in-the-application.md`]
- **Use a durable queue only to assign serial ownership.** Use an established durable queue only when an invariant crosses process boundaries and the domain can assign one partition or consumer serial ownership. [`invariants/use-a-durable-queue-only-to-assign-serial-ownership.md`]
- **Give a guarded lifecycle one pure decider.** Give an entity one pure decider answering "may this action happen now, and if not, why?" and listing open actions when all four hold: its lifecycle is a small closed state set (an enum, or a few flags and dates), several user actions depend on that state, several use cases and the page need the answer, and I/O facts are loaded first and passed in. [`invariants/give-a-guarded-lifecycle-one-pure-decider.md`]
- **Use a smaller tool when no decider fits.** When any of a decider's four conditions fails (small closed state set, multiple state-dependent user actions, needed across multiple use cases and the UI, pure once I/O facts are loaded), use the smaller tool: an inline guard (+ read-model flag if the UI needs it) for one action in one place; a read-model flag for a single yes/no; a plain pure function for one decision with 1–2 callers and no action list; conditional writes/constraints for system-driven transitions; a closed type mirroring external states; or the DB alone when it expresses the whole rule. [`invariants/use-a-smaller-tool-when-no-decider-fits.md`]
- **Pass state and time into a decider.** Pass plain state and time into a decider; it does no I/O (no clock, repository, or service) — load I/O facts first and pass them in. [`invariants/pass-state-and-time-into-a-decider.md`]
- **Take date rules from the organisation's business date.** A rule that depends on the date takes the business date, "today" in the organisation's time zone, from the one clock every caller uses, not a UTC date cut from the current instant. [`invariants/take-date-rules-from-the-organisations-business-date.md`]
- **Keep the state change out of the decider.** Put only the decision in the decider; keep the state change as a plain transform in the use case unless the transform itself is a rule. [`invariants/keep-the-state-change-out-of-the-decider.md`]
- **Pin a rule's SQL copy to the decider.** When SQL must mirror a decider rule (e.g., filtering a list by derived status), keep the SQL copy and pin it to the decider with a parity test. [`invariants/pin-a-rules-sql-copy-to-the-decider.md`]
- **Record a module's invariants beside its code.** Record a module's invariants in `invariants.yaml` at the module root, beside the code a change would break. [`invariants/record-a-modules-invariants-beside-its-code.md`]
- **Record only invariants a newcomer could break.** Give an invariant an entry only when a capable newcomer could break it with a reasonable-looking change; a rule a type makes unrepresentable, or a database constraint arbitrates, needs none. [`invariants/record-only-invariants-a-newcomer-could-break.md`]
- **Record only rules that are enforced and proved.** Add an `invariants.yaml` entry only when the rule is both enforced and proved, with non-empty `owner` and `proof` lists of bare symbol or path strings, and never loosen the schema for unproved rules. [`invariants/record-only-rules-that-are-enforced-and-proved.md`]
- **Give every invariant entry an id and five fields.** Each `invariants.yaml` file holds a top-level `invariants` sequence with no file-level intro prose and no unknown keys, where every entry has required `id` (`[A-Z]+(?:-[A-Z]+)*-\d{3}`, repo-unique and never renumbered once cited), present-tense `title`, `rule`, `why`, and non-empty bare symbol/path lists `owner` and `proof`, plus optional `accepts` and `related`. [`invariants/give-every-invariant-entry-an-id-and-five-fields.md`]
- **Write an invariant as it holds now.** Write the rule as it holds now and edit the entry when it changes; history lives in version control, and the file is not a decision log. [`invariants/write-an-invariant-as-it-holds-now.md`]
- **Confirm the proof fails without the owner.** Before listing symbols in `owner` or `proof`, open both and confirm each `proof` check fails if its `owner` boundary stops enforcing the rule. [`invariants/confirm-the-proof-fails-without-the-owner.md`]
- **Record a cross-module invariant in each owner.** A rule that spans modules is recorded by each module that enforces part of it, with each entry naming its own `owner` boundary and listing the other modules' rule IDs in `related`. [`invariants/record-a-cross-module-invariant-in-each-owner.md`]
- **Test behaviour, not call sequences.** Assert what happened (outputs, state changes, and side effects that matter), not how the code was called or the order of its internal calls, unless that order is itself the behaviour. [`tests/test-behaviour-not-call-sequences.md`]
- **Use real dependencies first, fakes second, mocks last.** Prefer the real dependency when cheap enough, a hand-written fake when the real thing is too heavy, slow, or unstable, and a library mock only at a narrow, volatile boundary — never default to mocks. [`tests/use-real-dependencies-first-fakes-second-mocks-last.md`]
- **Test through the real boundary when you can.** Test cross-boundary behaviour through the real wiring and flow rather than an isolated unit with mocked wiring. [`tests/test-through-the-real-boundary-when-you-can.md`]
- **Match the test level to the failure risk.** Match test level to failure risk — unit test for pure decisions, behaviour test through ports for orchestration, real-adapter integration test for persistence/protocol, composition test for wiring, and a few end-to-end tests for critical journeys; follow no fixed pyramid or coverage quota. [`tests/match-the-test-level-to-the-failure-risk.md`]
- **Test pure code directly.** Test a pure function (a transform, calculation, rule, validator, or mapping) directly, with no host, mount, or stand-in. [`tests/test-pure-code-directly.md`]
- **Test an adapter directly only when it has behaviour.** Test an adapter directly when it is non-trivial, its mapping or failure handling matters, or the external API is brittle; never write tests that only restate the ORM or SDK. [`tests/test-an-adapter-directly-only-when-it-has-behaviour.md`]
- **Enforce module boundaries with a check that runs.** Enforce module boundaries (`Modules/` isolation) with a check that runs in the build or CI, not a document. [`tests/enforce-module-boundaries-with-a-check-that-runs.md`]
- **Give every different outcome a test.** Test every materially different outcome at the cheapest honest level; multiple branches yielding one outcome don't each need a test, and wiring tests don't cover the use case behind them. [`tests/give-every-different-outcome-a-test.md`]
- **Add a test only for behaviour nothing else proves.** A test earns its place by proving behaviour no other test proves, at the cheapest level that proves it. [`tests/add-a-test-only-for-behaviour-nothing-else-proves.md`]
- **Extend an existing test before writing a new one.** Extend an existing test before writing a new one for new behaviour. [`tests/extend-an-existing-test-before-writing-a-new-one.md`]
- **Delete a test your change makes redundant.** A change that makes a test redundant deletes that test in the same change. [`tests/delete-a-test-your-change-makes-redundant.md`]
- **Never pin wording, styling, or layout in a test.** Do not assert exact wording, styling, colour, or layout; assert what the user can see or do, such as a message shown or a section revealed. [`tests/never-pin-wording-styling-or-layout-in-a-test.md`]
- **Mark an unfixed gap as an expected failure.** When a test hits a reported unfixed gap, mark it as an expected failure naming that work — never skip it — so the suite goes red when the gap is fixed and the mark gets removed. [`tests/mark-an-unfixed-gap-as-an-expected-failure.md`]
- **Count a fake as coverage only above the port.** A test using a fake or mock covers only behaviour above the port, never the replaced adapter; prove arbitration, atomicity, ordering, redelivery, and lock loss through the real adapter. [`tests/count-a-fake-as-coverage-only-above-the-port.md`]
- **Run one behaviour suite against fake and real adapter.** Where a fake could drift from the real adapter, run one shared behaviour suite against the fake and every real adapter. [`tests/run-one-behaviour-suite-against-fake-and-real-adapter.md`]
- **Type a stand-in response against the generated API types.** Type stand-in API responses against generated API types (`satisfies components["schemas"]["…"]` or a typed fixture helper) so API changes break tests at compile time. [`tests/type-a-stand-in-response-against-the-generated-api-types.md`]
- **Reach a fake's failures through trigger values.** In an end-to-end journey, reach a fake's failure modes through agreed trigger values in the fake, not by intercepting the page's requests. [`tests/reach-a-fakes-failures-through-trigger-values.md`]
- **Keep end-to-end journeys simple and stable.** Keep each end-to-end journey simple and happy-path first, with role or test-id selectors, no sleeps, and no state shared between tests. [`tests/keep-end-to-end-journeys-simple-and-stable.md`]
- **Coordinate concurrency tests without sleeps.** Drive concurrency-test actors in a fixed order using barriers, hooks, or controlled transactions — never timing sleeps. [`tests/coordinate-concurrency-tests-without-sleeps.md`]
- **Assert the durable outcome of a race.** Run concurrency tests at the real arbitrating boundary (DB, queue, or workflow engine) and assert durable outcomes for winner, loser, retries, and conflicts — not mock method calls. [`tests/assert-the-durable-outcome-of-a-race.md`]
- **Judge test code by the testing rules only.** Test code may import whatever it needs and is judged by the testing rules (double names, mock density, location), not by the production rules on layer purity, module shape, or .NET style. [`tests/judge-test-code-by-the-testing-rules-only.md`]
- **Test frontend logic, composables, and pages before components.** On the frontend, test pure `logic/` directly, composables where state or orchestration matters, and pages where wiring matters, rather than making presentational components the main test surface. [`tests/test-frontend-logic-composables-and-pages-before-components.md`]
- **Test what the user can do in a UI.** Test a user interface by what the user can accomplish and understand (prerequisites and ordering, the common path, what is revealed, visible outcomes and previews, consequences, and validation and recovery guidance), not by its control layout or implementation terms. [`tests/test-what-the-user-can-do-in-a-ui.md`]
